results.text:
One week since we launched dots! 

We’ve been working through your feedback and shipped a bunch of improvements:
- Faster cloud browsing
- Fixed extra phone notifications while you’re already using ChatGPT
- Cleaner code blocks and attachments on web
- Fewer pauses while waiting for a reply
- Faster sidebar loading, smoother animations and less loading jank
- Fixed character rendering in Safari and Firefox
- Fixed Outlook setup getting stuck
- Clearer plan guidance + a way to retry failed activity loads
- More stable safety banners on web
- Fixed clipped approval buttons and oversized Gmail previews hiding approvals
- Fixed enterprise access issues on web and when starting voice
- Better dot organization of when to use new versus existing codex threads

Up next:
- Voice reliability (being improved everyday, but we’ll shout when it’s up to par with our expectations)
- Increasing dot’s control of your Codex app: manage project folders, have full Codex thread context, rename threads, and more
- Better organization to know what your dot is working on at any given moment
- Connect your dot to multiple computers
- Better Windows support for local computer control
- what else?

Thanks for trying our product and giving us lots of feedback. Keep it coming!

results.text:
i just automated our release and QA process!
using Grok Bot i made two Team Bots: sandcastle, my release manager, and poteto, my engineer bot. i added them to Slack and made a new channel for managing releases.

first i tell sandcastle that i want to do a cut. it'll DM all the contributors with links to their PRs so they know what goes in the next release and can DM the bot back if they have any blockers or objections.

sandcastle then kicks off the build, watches it automatically, and starts up an automated fuzz swarm. usually this is 10+ agents running on Grok 4.7 xhigh to run the build, click around and use it like a real user (using our verification skills and feature map), some are directed while a few are "chaos monkey" clicking things randomly to see what breaks. 

whenever it finds an issue, i tell it to @ mention my engineer bot poteto, to spin up a Cursor Project to own triaging and fixing all the high pri issues. depending on the severity i may ask it to cherry pick the fix into our release branch and cut a patch release, or if it's a pre-existing issue i still fix it but include in the next release instead

that's one more tedious task that Grok Bot now handles for our team
